name: Epoetin alfa
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 50 to 100 Units/kg 3 times weekly IV or SC; IV route recommended in hemodialysis; individualize maintenance
40,000 Units weekly or 150 Units/kg 3 times weekly

usual_adult_dose.indication: Reduction of allogeneic transfusion in surgery
usual_adult_dose.dose: 300 Units/kg/day for 15 days or 600 Units/kg weekly

common: CKD (≥5%): hypertension, arthralgia, muscle spasm, pyrexia, dizziness, medical device malfunction, vascular occlusion, upper respiratory tract infection
serious: Death, myocardial infarction, stroke, venous thromboembolism, vascular access thrombosis (boxed warning; risk higher when targeting hemoglobin >11 g/dL)
Tumor progression or shortened survival in cancer

contraindications: Pure red cell aplasia after any erythropoietin protein drug
Serious allergic reactions to epoetin alfa
Multiple-dose vials (benzyl alcohol): neonates, infants, pregnant and lactating women
monitoring: Hemoglobin at least weekly when starting or adjusting, then at least monthly; do not raise the dose more often than every 4 weeks
Iron status before and during treatment
Dialysis prescription and heparinization may need adjustment (label 5.11)

pk.half_life: 4 to 13 hours after IV dosing in CKD
pk.half_life_eskd: Similar on and off dialysis in adults with serum creatinine >3 mg/dL (label)
pk.dialyzability: Not stated; half-life similar on and off dialysis (label).
